title: Conceding and contrasting
description: Concede a point and set two facts against each other.

blocks.text: To concede a point, Polish uses chociaż, or the more formal mimo że and choć, each followed by a clause; mimo and pomimo on their own take a noun in the genitive: mimo deszczu. Wprawdzie announces a concession that ale or lecz then answers. To set two facts side by side, use natomiast or z kolei, which often stand after the first element of their clause. Niemniej jednak means nevertheless.
Chociaż był zmęczony, pracował do północy.
blocks.translation: Although he was tired, he worked until midnight.

blocks.text: Mimo że padało, mecz się odbył.
blocks.translation: Even though it was raining, the match took place.
Despite the rain, the match took place.
blocks.note: Mimo without że takes a noun in the genitive.

blocks.text: Wprawdzie projekt jest drogi, ale przyniesie duże oszczędności.
blocks.translation: The project is admittedly expensive, but it will bring large savings.

blocks.text: Wyniki są dobre. Niemniej jednak nie możemy spocząć na laurach.
blocks.translation: The results are good. Nevertheless, we cannot rest on our laurels.

lines.speaker: Dyrektor
lines.translation: Should we open a second branch?

lines.speaker: Analityczka
lines.text: Wprawdzie koszty są wysokie, ale rynek rośnie.
lines.translation: The costs are admittedly high, but the market is growing.

lines.speaker: Analityczka
lines.text: Konkurencja jest silna w stolicy, na południu natomiast prawie jej nie ma.
lines.translation: Competition is strong in the capital, whereas in the south there is almost none.
